items.title: Baseline SSRF denial cases are explicit
items.statement: The fixture explicitly denies metadata, localhost, loopback, IPv6 link-local, one RFC1918 address, file URLs, private redirects, and a modeled DNS-rebind result; this is meaningful baseline egress coverage.

items.title: Permission asks and visible policy cards are represented
items.statement: Search and research wildcard scopes, host-scoped fetch/crawl operations, visible ask cards, and explicit deny cards are represented rather than silently inferred.

items.title: Robots, fanout, and depth controls have denial reasons
items.statement: The fixture requires robots denials and named fanout/depth cap outcomes, providing a baseline for crawl policy enforcement.

items.title: Raw-secret projection and redaction failure cases exist
items.statement: The fixture rejects raw credential projection, unredacted URL tokens, missing artifact redaction status, and failed artifact redaction, and requires cache metadata indicating secret checks.

items.title: Citation and planning lineage negatives are represented
items.statement: Snippet-only citations are rejected, planning research requires read/citation references plus a plan or ledger source reference, and runtime work-manifest types are expressly excluded.

items.title: Private-host classification lacks normalization and address-family adversaries
items.statement: The egress set samples one RFC1918 address and several special forms but does not falsify the classifier with 172.16/12, 192.168/16, carrier-grade NAT, IPv6 ULA, IPv4-mapped IPv6, integer/octal/hex IPv4, trailing-dot hosts, userinfo, IDNA, or mixed-case/canonicalization variants.
items.impact: Alternative encodings can bypass SSRF controls while the fixture suite remains green.
items.builder_discretion: Add table-driven deny fixtures for all non-public ranges and parser-equivalent host representations.

items.title: DNS and redirect checks are modeled as static facts, not lifecycle invariants
items.statement: A prefilled resolved_ip and one redirect target do not test DNS pinning across preflight, connection, retries, redirect hops, or multiple A/AAAA answers; no fixture exercises a public-to-private time-of-check/time-of-use transition.
items.impact: A rebind or redirect-chain race could reach private infrastructure after an allowed preflight.

items.title: Host permission derivation may overgrant sibling hosts
items.statement: A URL on docs.example.com is normalized to https://example.com/*, but no negative fixture proves whether expanding to the registrable domain is intentional or prevents reuse by untrusted sibling subdomains, alternate ports, downgraded schemes, or lookalike domains.
items.impact: A grant for one host could silently authorize a broader origin set than the user saw.

items.title: Approval lifecycle and concurrent policy changes are untested
items.statement: Ask/deny fixtures describe a point decision but omit grant expiry, one-shot versus persistent grants, cancellation, revocation, policy changes while a request is queued, duplicate concurrent asks, and reuse of cached grants by a different caller or run.
items.impact: Execution may continue under stale or cross-run authority after the user or policy has withdrawn permission.

items.title: Policy precedence and private-host approval authority are unspecified
items.statement: The localhost case name mentions lack of explicit private-host approval, yet its expected outcome is unconditional denial; the fixture does not state whether such approval exists, who can grant it, or how it composes with strict no-network, run-mode, enterprise, and tool policies.
items.impact: Implementations can disagree on whether a user grant overrides a stronger deny or whether private egress is ever authorizable.

items.title: Failed redaction has no quarantine or rollback oracle
items.statement: Missing and failed redaction are rejected, but no fixture requires removal of already-written bytes, quarantine of derivatives, suppression from previews/indexes/sync, or atomic rollback when persistence partly succeeds.
items.impact: Sensitive artifacts can remain reachable after the validator reports the expected error.

items.title: Cache privacy lifecycle is reduced to field presence
items.statement: The cache case requires ttl_seconds, a boolean no-secret assertion, and a redaction profile ID but omits TTL bounds, expiry enforcement, eviction, user deletion, per-principal isolation, encryption, revalidation, stale-data behavior, and downstream copy cleanup.
items.impact: Secret-bearing or user-specific web content can persist, leak across principals, or outlive its declared retention.

items.title: Redaction coverage does not test sensitive surfaces or transformations
items.statement: Only one query token and status flags are exercised; fixtures omit URL fragments and userinfo, cookies, request/response headers and bodies, DOM text, OCR, form fields, storage, console output, HAR exports, encoded secrets, and derivatives such as thumbnails or recordings.
items.impact: A redaction_status of success may coexist with sensitive content on untested artifact surfaces.

items.title: Offline and transport failure states are absent
items.statement: A policy deny and runtime-unavailable state do not cover DNS failure, timeout, TLS/certificate failure, captive portal, proxy authentication, connection reset, mid-stream loss, retry exhaustion, or transition between online and offline during fetch/crawl.
items.impact: UI and evidence can report policy denial, success, or completeness for transient transport failures and partial responses.

items.title: Crawl limits omit aggregate, byte, time, and concurrent budgets
items.statement: Per-request page and depth caps do not constrain response bytes, decompression expansion, redirects, total wall time, total domains, concurrent crawls, global tenant budgets, or races in which several workers each pass the same remaining-budget check.
items.impact: A compliant implementation can exhaust memory, bandwidth, storage, or remote-service capacity while passing the fixture.

items.title: Visible-card booleans do not guarantee truthful GUI state
items.statement: must_show_card and visible_card assert presence only; no fixture requires the card to show the effective policy source, exact scope, target host, partial progress, denial versus offline distinction, stale status, safe actions, or terminal outcome.
items.impact: Users can approve an unclear scope or be misled about why a call failed or whether partial results are complete.

items.title: Security and remediation cards lack accessibility negatives
items.statement: No fixture requires accessible names and descriptions, keyboard operation, focus management, screen-reader announcement of ask/deny transitions, non-color status cues, contrast, reduced motion, or usable zoom/reflow for permission and prompt-injection chips.
items.impact: Assistive-technology users may not perceive or safely act on security-critical states.

items.title: Localization and bidirectional-text security are untested
items.statement: Expected reasons are machine tokens, but no fixture covers localized card copy, long expansion, pluralization, RTL layouts, Unicode domain rendering, bidi controls, locale-sensitive case folding, or a stable separation between display text and policy identifiers.
items.impact: Localized UI may truncate the operative reason or render a deceptive host/scope while the policy engine evaluates another string.

evidence.exact_quote: "purpose": "Validator-facing negative fixtures for web permission, security, cache, citation, and browser-unavailable coverage.",

items.title: Schema compatibility and artifact migration have no negative cases
items.statement: The document declares v1 but contains no fixture for unknown schema IDs, older/newer producers, missing newly required fields, unknown enum values, preserved error semantics, or migration of cached permissions, evidence, and browser artifacts.
items.impact: Upgrades may silently accept insecure legacy records, reject recoverable data, or reinterpret authority and redaction states.

items.title: Evidence recording lacks operational and support invariants
items.statement: Two crawl cases require evidence and several cases name reasons, but fixtures do not require correlation IDs, policy/version provenance, timestamps, caller identity, redirect/DNS decision trace, retry count, partial-result counts, redaction profile version, or support-safe diagnostics.
items.impact: Operators cannot reconstruct a denial, leak, partial crawl, or policy race without exposing sensitive data in ad hoc logs.

items.title: Remediation actions have no destructive-action guardrail
items.statement: The runtime-unavailable fixture requires remediation action IDs but does not distinguish safe diagnostics from installing software, resetting configuration, clearing browser data, deleting caches, changing policy, or restarting active work, and provides no confirmation/preview/rollback requirements.
items.impact: A visible remediation button may perform irreversible or authority-expanding actions without informed consent.

items.title: Planning evidence references are presence-only cross-document seams
items.statement: The fixture requires read, citation, and ledger-or-plan references but does not prove that refs resolve, are hash-bound to the cited source, belong to the same invocation and authority context, survive migration, or cannot point to deleted, stale, or unrelated evidence.
items.impact: A planning record can pass validation with dangling or semantically unrelated evidence references.

items.title: Several expected outcomes are non-falsifiable unions or field-presence checks
items.statement: partial_or_denied and fanout_or_depth_capped permit materially different behaviors, while must_require and must_not do not define type, value, ordering, exclusivity, or postcondition; a validator can pass incompatible implementations.
items.impact: Green fixtures do not establish a single observable contract for partial results, cap attribution, remediation, or evidence shape.

items.title: Malformed and ambiguous fixture inputs are missing
items.statement: All cases are structurally valid and use known strings; no negative tests cover missing/duplicate case IDs, nulls in required fields, wrong types, unknown tools/surfaces/reasons, contradictory must_require and must_not, duplicate keys, oversized strings, control characters, or invalid URLs.
items.impact: Parser differentials or fail-open handling of malformed policy artifacts can escape test coverage.

items.title: Prompt-injection handling asserts visibility but not containment
items.statement: Visible chips and prohibition of hidden system-prompt merging do not test active-content isolation, tool-call suppression, instruction/data provenance, nested or encoded injection, content copied into later prompts, or user override and acknowledgement semantics.
items.impact: An injection can remain operationally effective while still producing the required chip.

items.title: Citation validity is tested only at the snippet/read boundary
items.statement: Rejecting snippet-only evidence does not falsify citations to a read page that changed, did not contain the claim, is paywalled or dynamically rendered, was truncated, has conflicting versions, or was read under a different URL after redirects.
items.impact: Consumers can accept a formally read-backed citation that does not support the presented claim.

items.title: Unmodeled egress intermediaries may invalidate host-level assumptions
items.statement: The window does not establish behavior when a system proxy, service worker, browser extension, alternate resolver, HTTP CONNECT tunnel, or native-browser helper performs resolution or redirects outside the policy component's observation boundary.
items.impact: A second egress path may bypass otherwise correct URL and DNS policy checks.

dimension_assessments.summary: Citation consumers and alternate egress/browser intermediaries lack negative contracts.
Malformed records, approval revocation, transport transitions, and redaction persistence transitions are absent.
DNS TOCTOU, concurrent approval reuse, and shared crawl-budget races are untested.
Transport, crawl, redaction, and persistence partial failures lack deterministic postconditions.
Failed redaction and remediation have no cleanup, retry, compensation, or rollback oracles.
Scope expansion, grant lifecycle, precedence, and private-host approval authority are underspecified.
Baseline secret rejection exists, but cache and artifact retention, isolation, cleanup, and derivative handling are missing.
Host encodings, malformed policy records, active content, and prompt-injection containment are incomplete.
Card presence is asserted, but truthful scope, reason, progress, staleness, and terminal-state presentation are not.
Policy denial and runtime absence exist, but offline and transport failure states do not.
Page/depth baselines exist; aggregate bytes, time, concurrency, decompression, and storage budgets are absent.
No security-critical card or chip accessibility acceptance oracle is present.
Localized strings, expansion, RTL, bidi, Unicode host rendering, and locale-independent policy IDs are untested.
The v1 declaration has no producer-version, unknown-field, legacy-record, or migration fixtures.
Named reasons and evidence booleans exist, but reconstructable, privacy-safe operational traces do not.
Remediation action IDs are required without confirmation, preview, privilege, or rollback constraints.
Planning and evidence references are presence-only and lack resolution, integrity, context, and lifecycle checks.
Union outcomes and field-presence assertions permit incompatible observable behaviors.
Egress intermediaries outside the modeled policy boundary may bypass its host and DNS assumptions.
